title: Acton Survey
primary_metric: Jeff's total personal call time (hours) -- learner interviews plus every guide-coordination call each sampling method actually requires -- to complete a 142-learner (10%) survey of the 1,420-learner, 50-campus Acton network within his 3-month runway

options.A: Simple Random Sample -- the simplest method to administer: one flat draw of 1,420 IDs, no per-campus quotas to track, while Jeff places every 15-20-minute call himself, one at a time
options.B: Stratified Sample -- more calls and coordination required, but it corrects for wildly uneven campus sizes so small and large campuses are proportionally represented

legacy_conversion_note: Original source (source/Y2/Session 5/Acton Survey/Case Study_ Acton Survey.docx + Guide Notes.docx + the real 2021 roster xlsx) is a real Acton-network dilemma -- Jeff and Laura Sandefer's retirement-driven mascot survey, Xander Morgan as the statistician, the personal-phone-call methodology (Jeff calls the guide, the guide facilitates the learner call), the 15-20-minute-per-call constraint, and the 'campuses with at least two studios' eligibility rule are all preserved verbatim from the source docx. The 1,420-learner, 50-campus roster (source: '2021 Learners At Campuses With At Least Two Studios_ ID Numbers, Gender, Age and Location.xlsx') is real, complete 2021 data -- every campus size, percentage, and stratified allocation figure in case.md Appendix B/C is computed directly from that real spreadsheet, not invented (see RESEARCH_LOG.md for the exact computation). Per the human-approved dilemma lock (cases/_concepts/LEGACY_DILEMMA_LOCKS_2026-08-20.md), the original 5-option dilemma (Simple Random / Stratified / Systematic / Cluster / a combination) is narrowed to the two options with the clearest real tradeoff: Simple Random Sample vs. Stratified Sample. The original case asked students to freely pick a sample size and administer their own method with no quantitative comparison point; this conversion adds the load-bearing quantitative spine the original lacked -- a fixed target sample size (142 = 10% of the real population, a stated case premise, not an external citation), an exact hypergeometric probability model (computed from the real campus-size list, not estimated) of how many of the 50 real campuses would receive zero calls under Option A, and a largest-remainder proportional allocation table for Option B (also computed from the real data, citing the real historical Hamilton's-method apportionment technique). The primary_metric (Jeff's total personal call-time) and its balance are new modeling built to make the locked dilemma's own stated rationale for each option (A = simpler/faster administration; B = corrects for uneven campus size) quantitatively checkable, per SPEC §2.

deliverables.text: A population-and-sample description: total eligible population, how the 142-learner target sample was derived, and what percent of the population it represents.
A condensed campus roster table: all 50 eligible campuses, learner count, and percent of total population.

A Simple Random Sample risk analysis: probability that a simple random sample of 142 contains zero learners from a given campus, for at least 3 campuses of different sizes, plus the network-wide expected shutout count.
A Stratified Sample allocation table for all 50 campuses, reconciled to sum to exactly 142.
A total call-time comparison (hours) for each option, checked against Jeff's 3-month runway.
Two original visual displays: total call-time by option, and network coverage (% of 50 campuses reached) by option.

balance.argument_a: Option A (Simple Random Sample) wins the graded primary metric -- Jeff's total personal call time is lower under A than under B, because A only pays a guide-coordination call for however many campuses happen to land learners in the random draw (an expected 39.2 of 50, not all 50), while B pays for a coordination call at all 50 campuses by construction. Beyond the hours themselves, A carries a real operational advantage the call-time metric doesn't even capture: Jeff is running this whole survey alone, one call at a time, with no team to divide the bookkeeping. SRS needs only one flat list of 1,420 IDs and a single random draw of 142 -- nothing to track campus-by-campus. Stratified requires Jeff to carry 50 separate running quotas simultaneously (Appendix C's largest-remainder allocation table), each needing its own tally of interviews-completed-vs-target as calls trickle in over three months, with real risk of over- or under-shooting a campus's target along the way. That per-campus coordination overhead is a genuine administrative cost distinct from raw hours. SRS also gives every individual learner network-wide an equal, unbiased chance of being called, which is a real and legitimate fairness argument in its own right (equal voice per learner, not per campus).
balance.argument_b: Option B (Stratified Sample) guarantees every one of the network's 50 campuses is actually heard -- zero campuses silenced by chance. Under Option A, each of the network's 37 dozen-learner campuses independently carries a real, computed 28.1% probability of contributing zero learners to the sample (Appendix C, exact hypergeometric), and the expected number of campuses receiving zero calls network-wide (about 10.8 of 50 -- roughly one in five) is large enough that a real fraction of the network goes unheard on a survey whose entire stated premise (Background) is giving every age of learner a voice. B closes that gap completely for a small amount of extra call time.
balance.margin_basis: Total call time (hours) for each option = 142 learner-interview calls x 17.5 min (Appendix D, MA2) + (campuses reached) x 15 min (Appendix D, MA1). B reaches all 50 campuses by construction; A reaches an expected 50 - 10.765 = 39.235 campuses (Appendix C's exact hypergeometric sum, computed from the real 50-campus size list in Appendix B). Total_A = (142x17.5 + 39.235x15)/60 = 51.23 h. Total_B = (142x17.5 + 50x15)/60 = 53.92 h. margin_pct = (Total_B - Total_A)/Total_A x 100 = 5.25%, rounded to 5.3%.

derived.note: All four figures are computed from the real 50-campus size list (case.md Appendix B) via the exact hypergeometric formula (Appendix C) and Appendix D's stated call-time assumptions (MA1, MA2). See sensitivity_model.py for the runnable computation and RESEARCH_LOG.md for the derivation.

modeling_assumptions.basis: No public figure exists for an internal Acton-network scheduling call of this kind (WebSearch on 2026-08-20 found no citable source for average school administrative scheduling call duration). This case uses the low end of the case's own real, stated 15-20 minute learner-call bracket (Appendix A), since a coordination call carries no interview content -- it is purely scheduling logistics -- and is realistically shorter than a full learner interview.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: The answer is sensitive to this value -- see sensitivity_model.py FLEX. Pushing it to the top of the case's own stated 15-20 minute bracket (20 min, not a fabricated value outside that range) still does not flip the primary-metric winner for this case (verified below); it widens both options' totals, but B's grows faster than A's (B pays the extra minutes across all 50 campuses, A across only the expected 39.235 it reaches), so A's margin actually grows slightly (5.25% -> 6.58%).
